messages:
Alice: spotted a weird microburst in the p99s on canary yesterday during the 11:20 load test. short, ~30-90ms spikes but CPU and GPU util both looked okay.
Bob: can you paste the trace? nsys timeline would help. did it line up with batch boundary events?
Alice: pasted below — big chunk from nsys + perfetto. main oddity: kernel choice flipback inside the window, seemed to rebind kernel variant mid-request.
perf-bot: upload complete: https://perf-storage/reports/2050009999/nsys.tar.gz :eyes:
Carla: quick take: that "flipback" sounds like scheduler preemption causing kernel to be relaunched on a different stream/kernel path. could also be KV cache miss causing extra memcpy + small-kernel fallback.
Dan: I looked at the nvprof samples — there's a ~1.2ms hitch where we run a narrow-matmul fallback then resume wide-matmul. timeline shows queue->compute->queue->compute for the same request.
Eva: that pattern will wreck tail latency if continuous batching window tries to combine a late arrival request and then we pick a different kernel due to seq len heuristic. Did we recently change kernel-selection thresholds?
Alice: not intentionally in this branch. but optimizer PR 782 bumped the heuristic for transposed gemm threshold. might be related.
Bob: repro steps I ran:
```
# reproduce locally with small window
./run_trace.sh --model rdx-7b --load 500rps --batch-window-ms 8 --seed 42
nsys profile --output ns_report --trace=nvtx ./serve_canary
```
Repro shows periodic 50-120ms p99 spikes every ~3000 reqs.
Carla: interestingly the KV cache hit rate during spikes drops from 97% to 63% in the trace. that suggests a cache thrash that triggers a different codepath (prefetch miss path).
Dan: where in the pipeline is the cache eviction happening? prefetch sweep? or TTL?
Alice: our KV sweeper runs on a timer and we had lowered the sweep threshold in the canary config to be more aggressive. might be evicting prefixes mid-batch.
Eva: hypothesis: aggressive KV sweep + small microburst arrival causes an incoming request to miss prefix in cache, runtime picks conservative kernel (to minimize memory pressure), then after cache refill we switch back => double-work and queue churn.
Bob: to test: 1) disable KV sweeper on canary 2) force persistent cache for the failing prefix 3) reduce batch-window to avoid mixing late arrivals.
Carla: also produce a perfetto flame for a single spike. export slices: NVTX marks show kernel variant names: fast_gemm_xf32, fallback_gemm_int8, and a memcpy_in between. that memcpy aligns with the cache miss duration.
Dan: I can instrument kernel-selection decision with a light-weight log to capture reason codes (e.g., "qdepth-based", "prefetch-miss", "seq-threshold"). add a tag to nvtx with reason.
Alice: that would be great. add a short ID so we can correlate across devices. please try on canary.
perf-bot: scheduled run: 2050010200 with nvtx_reason=true and kv_sweeper=false
Eva: short-term mitigation: bump cache size and set sweeper cooldown +1s; long-term: make the kernel selection stable within a request (do not flip variants mid-request), fall back to queued re-scheduling instead.
Bob: agree. also add a metric: "kernel-switchback_count" per request. if >0 for p99 requests, alert.
Carla: next steps action items:
- Dan: add nvtx reason tags + unique req id (ETA today)
- Alice: run reproduce with sweeper off + larger cache (ETA this afternoon)
- Bob: add telemetry probe for kernel-switchback_count (ETA EOD)
- Eva: draft rollback for heuristic PR 782 in case we confirm root cause (ETA tomorrow morning)
Alice: thanks all. will post the nsys/perfetto snippets in the thread when I have them.
Bob: and add a small unit test that ensures no variant churn for a single request (simulate sequence lengths that cross threshold).
Carla: FYI I also see a small host-side CPU spin between kernel launches ~100-200us, likely from stream synchronization. could be coalesced by using an async memcpy pipeline.
Dan: will try switching to cudaMemcpyAsync + dedicated copy stream in the probe. might reduce the mid-kernel gap.
Eva: if mitigations reduce p99 but not eliminate, we'll opt for "stable kernel per request" policy and then tune selection offline.
Alice: logging the perf-bot run id: 2050010200. I'll upload the perfetto flame and trimmed nsys timeline into the perf board.
perf-bot: upload complete: https://perf-storage/reports/2050010200/perfetto_flame.html :white_check_mark:
Alice: closing loop — thanks team, this is looking actionable.
